title: Neko-TOP case file
description: Neko's case file plus the keys of the Neko-TOP drivers. Everything Neko's own schema accepts outside Neko-TOP's keys stays accepted.

unsteady.description: Run the optimisation with an unsteady forward and adjoint solve. Default false. Read by the topology optimisation drivers only (sources/simulation/simulation.f90:271).

state_recovery.description: How the forward state is recovered for the adjoint; read, and required, only when `unsteady` is true.

norm_scaling.description: Left over from the power iteration, which has no caller; read at the document root. Default 0.5. Read only by the topology optimisation drivers (adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:468-491); typed under `optimization`.

norm_target.description: As `norm_scaling`. Default -1.0. Read only by the topology optimisation drivers (adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:468-491); typed under `optimization`.

norm_tolerance.description: As `norm_scaling`. Default 10.0. Read only by the topology optimisation drivers (adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:468-491); typed under `optimization`.

output_file.description: Left over from the power iteration; read at the document root by the topology optimisation drivers only (adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:468-491), where it must end in a file suffix Neko knows. Default `power_iterations.csv`.

case.description: Neko-TOP additions to Neko's open `case` object.

allOf.$comment: steady_simcomp.f90:148-151 aborts when a steady component meets more than one scalar. The component is registered by every driver (neko_top_register_types), so the rule holds without `optimization` too. It counts the entries of case.scalars; the code counts the enabled ones, so the rare [enabled, disabled] form is rejected too (the whitelisted keywords have no `contains`). With case.scalar present Neko builds that one and never reads case.scalars (neko src/case.f90:319-353), so the rule does not apply then. An entry with is_user true is skipped by Neko's factory (simulation_component_fctry.f90:108-109), so it is not counted.

optimizing.description: Restrictions that apply when the case has an `optimization` object, that is when a topology optimisation driver runs it.

allOf.$comment: neko_ext.f90:356-359 (reset_adjoint) reads case.adjoint_fluid.initial_condition at every design iteration with no fallback. adjoint_case.f90:452-459 reads output_value for the output controls that need it (and the adjoint fluid is built by the topology optimisation drivers only).

numerics.$comment: adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:309 and adjoint_case.f90:136 read these as JSON integers (no constants name); advection_adjoint_fctry.f90:96-99 reads the polynomial order the same way; a true `oifs` aborts (advection_adjoint_fctry.f90:105, adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:741). dealiased_polynomial_order is conditional, below.

allOf.$comment: adjoint_case.f90:252-253 aborts after the whole initialisation when only case.adjoint_scalars is given and has entries.

adjoint_case.f90:180-183: without case.adjoint_scalar, case.adjoint_scalars takes the array branch, which calls params%info('case.scalars', n_children=...) without `found`. On a missing path json-fortran is left in an exception state, every later lookup fails and the next read, json_get('case.time') at :260, aborts with 'Parameter case.time missing from the case file' (also for an empty case.adjoint_scalars).

neko_ext.f90:236-238 and :399-423 reset the scalar and its adjoint at every design iteration; with an enabled scalar but no enabled adjoint scalar reset_adjoint dereferences an unallocated array (neko_ext.f90:404).
adjoint_case.f90:204 needs case.scalar; adjoint_scalar_scheme.f90:341 needs it enabled.
adjoint_case.f90:309-312 and neko_ext.f90:420-423 read initial_condition.type of an enabled adjoint scalar without a default; nothing reads case.adjoint_scalar without `optimization`.

adjoint_scalar_scheme.f90:281 reads primal_name (default s) and looks the field up by it (:341); the field is named case.scalar.name (Neko default s). That the two names are equal cannot be expressed; the cases that cannot match are rejected. The adjoint scalar must be enabled (adjoint_case.f90:175-196); a disabled one never reads primal_name.
Same lookup: with the scalar named s (explicitly or by default) primal_name can only be s. Again only for an enabled adjoint scalar.

adjoint_case.f90:443-445 reads case.nsamples for output_control `org` with no default (neko src/common/case_file_utils.f90:129-142, json_utils.f90:252). Neko has the same rule for case.fluid.output_control.

advection_adjoint_fctry.f90:100-101 reads the order as a JSON integer, but only after the dummy-advection return (:85-94), which the adjoint takes when case.fluid.advection is false (adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:437-443) and, for the adjoint scalar, when case.adjoint_scalar.advection is false (adjoint_scalar_pnpn.f90:247-252). Otherwise Neko's own read, with its constants lookup, is the only one.

adjoint_scalar_scheme.f90:284-285,333-337 add the adjoint field only if no field of that name exists, else reuse it; the velocity and pressure fields and their adjoints exist before the adjoint scalar is set up (adjoint_fluid_scheme_incompressible.f90:198-200, adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:302). The adjoint then overwrites them, with no abort. The fields u_e, v_e, w_e (neko src/fluid/fluid_scheme_incompressible.f90:348-350) and u_adj_e, v_adj_e, w_adj_e (adjoint_fluid_scheme_incompressible.f90:360-362) exist too. The scheme's own fields abx1 and abx2 collide with the payload registered under the adjoint name (adjoint_scalar_pnpn.f90:215,217,263-267; neko src/common/checkpoint_payload.f90:607-611 aborts on a duplicate field name). The design fields design_indicator, brinkman_amplitude and sensitivity are registered after the adjoint scalar with ignore_existing (design_brinkman.f90:365-371; neko src/registries/registry.f90:258-260), so the design would silently get the scalar's field.

The same design fields (design_brinkman.f90:365-371, registered after sim%init with ignore_existing) alias a primal scalar of the same name: the scalar and the design overwrite each other with no abort.
Same: the primal scalar field is named `s` by default. Neko registers s_lambda, s_lambda_tot and s_cp for the scalar (neko src/scalar/scalar_scheme.f90:716-718).
Same: the fluid is named `fluid` by default and registers fluid_mu, fluid_mu_tot and fluid_rho (neko src/fluid/fluid_scheme_incompressible.f90:202,690-692).

adjoint_scalar_scheme.f90:281-285: the default name is primal_name//'_adj'; with primal_name u, v, w or p that is the adjoint velocity or pressure field, which the adjoint scalar then overwrites (:333-337).

neko_ext.f90:216-217 and :399-400 gate the scalar reset on case.scalar.enabled, which is absent for case.scalars, so a scalar of the array form is never re-initialised after the first design iteration (and has no adjoint scalar, adjoint_case.f90:177-190); only a disabled entry is accepted. With case.scalar present Neko builds that one and never reads case.scalars (neko src/case.f90:319-353), Neko-TOP reads case.scalars only in the adjoint_scalars branch of adjoint_case.f90:180-183 (not taken with case.adjoint_scalar) and its resets read case.scalar.enabled, so the rule applies only without case.scalar.

The adjoint velocity, pressure and scalar solvers build Neko's preconditioner through precon_factory (adjoint_fluid_scheme_incompressible.f90:318-326,345-347; adjoint_scalar_scheme.f90:292-299,388-390), and hsmg aborts for polynomial order 1 (neko src/krylov/pc_hsmg.f90:224-225). Neko's own rule covers the primal solvers (urn:neko:schema:case-file#/$defs/case/allOf/7).
brinkman_dissipation_objective.f90:150-162: both flags default to case.numerics.dealias and must end up equal, so a single flag must equal it.
brinkman_dissipation_objective.f90:150-162: both flags default to case.numerics.dealias and must end up equal, so a single flag must equal it.
scalar_mixing_objective_function.f90:171 aborts without an enabled adjoint scalar.
simulation.f90:283 aborts for an unsteady run with case.time.variable_timestep true.

Owner ruling 2026-11-16: a `steady` simulation component with `unsteady: true` is invalid. The rejection exists in the code only on an unmerged branch; steady_simcomp.f90:116-133 does not reject it yet. An entry with is_user true is skipped by Neko's factory before `type` is read (neko src/simulation_components/simulation_component_fctry.f90:108-109), so no steady component is built and the ruling does not apply to it (the overlay in simulation-components.schema.json exempts it too).

simulation.f90:271-301: `unsteady` is read at :271 and, for an unsteady run, state_recovery at :299 (factory :300-301); state_recovery is required for an unsteady run and not read otherwise. :283 aborts a variable timestep and :289-297 abort case.time.exact_output_time true. Read by the topology optimisation drivers only. problem.f90:615-626 maps the adjoint clock to the forward time as n_timesteps*dt - t_adj, which assumes the forward run starts at t = 0, while neko_ext.f90:128-129,321-322 reset both clocks to case.time.start_time: with a start_time above 0 the objective windows and the adjoint forcing gate the wrong steps and the sensitivity is wrong (zero in the probe).

start_time.$comment: A constants name is accepted next to the literal: Neko reads start_time with a constants lookup (neko src/common/time_state.f90:76) and Neko-TOP uses only the resolved value (neko_ext.f90:128-129,321-322). The value of a constant cannot be checked here, as for every lookup key.

allOf.$comment: case.restart_file breaks the same assumption as a start_time above 0: Neko's simulation_init restarts from the file on every call (neko src/simulation.f90:71-74), Neko-TOP calls it before every unsteady forward run (problem.f90:533), so the forward clock starts at the checkpoint time while backward samples use total_time - adjoint time (problem.f90:553,625). A windowed objective then selects different steps forward and backward and the sensitivity is wrong (run: 6.3e-2 error against 1.5e-2 without the window; the second part of that error is a known missing initial-state sample that a restart does not cause). Only the objective windows are rejected here; whether to reject unsteady + restart_file altogether is the owner's decision.

adjoint_fluid_pnpn.f90:468-491 reads these root keys (the power iteration leftovers) as JSON reals, and output_file with a file suffix that neko src/io/file.f90:133 knows. Without `optimization` nothing reads them.

The time-window test driver (tests/unit/objectives/time_window_tester.f90:128,137) aborts for a steady run and for an empty objective list. It also aborts for `pairwise: true` with an odd number of objectives (time_window_tester.f90:251-254), which the whitelisted keywords cannot express (no array-length parity).

time_window_tester.f90:199-202 aborts after the first run unless the fluid is frozen, and the only writers of fluid%freeze are the reset from case.fluid.freeze_flow (neko_ext.f90:267-270) and the steady simcomp (steady_simcomp.f90:283), which the schema does not allow in an unsteady run.
